_about: Explain's checks after the model, before anything is spoken (backend/llm/natlas_guard.py): an answer naming a medicine, or using a dose word, is never spoken; the page is read instead. Medicine names are the same in every language; dose words are per language. In a dose word, N stands for a number: digits (4, 0.5), a number word of that language (content/number_words/) or a range ('4 to 6', '4-6'); a hyphen may be there or not ('4-hourly', '4 hourly'). Medicine names and English dose words: reviewed and extended by Dr. Amos (17 Nov 2026); his reasons are in "_notes". Hausa, Yorùbá and Igbo dose words: drafts, for native speakers to review.

dose_abbreviations._about: Short dose words that are also ordinary words or letters ('bid', 'stat', 'daily', 'od', 'mane' as in a lion's mane). Each counts as a dose word only as a whole word right next to a number or a dose form ('1 tab bd', '500 mg tds', 'od x 5 days', 'bd for 7 days'), never on its own, so 'a bid to win' or 'daily life' is not blocked. Dr. Amos added the clinical shorthand (iv, im, sc, po, ac, pc, hs, qhs, sos, iu, q6h, q8h, q12h) and dotted forms (b.d., t.d.s., o.d., q.d.s.), 17 Nov 2026; these too count only next to a number or a dose form, so 'Chapter IV' or 'the PC lab' is not blocked.

dose_forms._about: Dose forms that make a short dose word count ('2 tabs bd'). Units are matched glued to a number too ('500mg tds').
